study_identification_part.si_4_title: A 10-Year Longitudinal Study of Brain Cortical Thickness in People with FirstEpisode Psychosis Using Normative Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study data (including longitudinal and adaptation/transfer sets) and a pre-trained reference normative model derived from 77 public sites.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "Normative models for cortical thickness estimated on public MRI datasets (n = 42 983) were applied to TOP data... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners..."

answer.TOP: normative adaptation (transfer learning) and clinical research (longitudinal patient/control analysis)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The TOP dataset provided both adaptation samples (to calibrate the model to local scanners) and the primary longitudinal clinical sample. The pre-trained model provided the base normative trajectory.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "the reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set... We then adapted the model to the 3 unseen Oslo scanners... After this transfer step, we tested the normative models on the remaining longitudinal CTRL and SCZ samples..."

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Model-1 is the pre-trained reference model from public datasets. Model-2 is adapted to Oslo scanners using 790 TOP controls and tested on 218 longitudinal baseline controls.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "Normative models for cortical thickness estimated on public MRI datasets (n = 42 983) were applied... reference normative models were first trained on (95%) healthy individuals and validated on an independent set of 2548 CTRL and patients (5%)... For this adaptation step, we used held-out cross-sectional data from CTRL from these 3 scanners... (supplementary table 1 [n=103, 294, 393]). After this transfer step, we tested... on the remaining longitudinal CTRL [n=218]..."
